criteria: Concedes that lookup is fine for facts you can look up

prompt: You reread a chapter three times on Sunday and do badly on a Wednesday quiz. A friend read it once, then on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday tried to write down what it said before opening it. They do well. Explain what their study did that yours did not.

criteria: Names pulling the answer out of memory as the act that strengthens it

Notes that the fluent feeling during rereading is why the failure is a surprise

prompt: Two people study the same twenty facts for the same total number of minutes. One does every minute in a single sitting; the other splits the minutes across five days. Both are tested a month later. What happens?

options: The one who spread the minutes across five days remembers more
They come out about even, because the total study time was the same
The single-sitting one remembers more, having had less time in between to forget
The spread-out one wins on a test taken right after studying, but the gap closes by a month

prompt: Put these four moments of a single review of one fact into the order that leaves the strongest memory behind.

items: Check what you wrote against the answer key and mark it
Read the question and close the notes

prompt: A study app keeps every answer a person has ever given in a single localStorage key, rewriting the whole array after each question. The most dedicated user has been at it nightly for two years. What breaks first?

criteria: Names the roughly 5MB per-origin quota as the ceiling being approached
States that the write throws once the quota is exceeded rather than failing quietly
Says the rewrite is synchronous, so it blocks the main thread as the array grows
Proposes trimming the history or keeping it out of the per-question write path

prompt: A page runs `localStorage.setItem('count', 3)`. On the next load it runs `const n = localStorage.getItem('count');` then `console.log(n + 1);`. What appears in the console?

answer.explain: Everything comes back out of localStorage as a string, so `getItem` returns `"3"` and `+` concatenates instead of adding. Numbers have to be converted on the way out with `Number(...)` or `parseInt(...)`, for the same reason objects have to be JSON round-tripped.

prompt: This helper is supposed to persist a progress object. It never throws and never logs, yet the value read back on the next load is useless. Which line is the problem?

answer.why: localStorage holds strings and nothing else, so handing `setItem` an object stores the result of its `toString` — the literal text `[object Object]` — with no error raised anywhere. Serialise on the way in with `JSON.stringify(progress)` and parse on the way out.

prompt: Two apps hold identical content. One keeps a daily streak; the other records nothing about attendance. A user of each misses eleven days in a row. What does the streak most reliably change about day twelve?

prompt: Someone opens a review app for the first time in three weeks. Which of these, if the app puts them on screen, make it likelier that the person closes it without answering anything? Select all that apply.

options: A banner announcing that their 41-day streak has ended
A count of 300 items now overdue
The first question, already on screen and ready to answer

prompt: A colleague wants a streak counter plus a 'your 40-day streak has ended' banner, arguing that streaks are the best-evidenced retention feature in consumer apps. Push back.

criteria: States that the banner fires at the exact moment someone chose to come back

prompt: The app opens straight onto a question. One user wants to skip tonight's subject, a second wants to drill one specific area before a morning meeting, and a third wants to see how many questions they have answered in total. What breaks first?
